lesson_title: The Equation That Lies — and How to Fix It
hook_text: This chemistry equation has correct formulas — and it is still LYING to you.
clip_script: Propane plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water. Every formula correct. Now count the atoms. Left side: three carbons, eight hydrogens, two oxygens. Right side: one carbon, two hydrogens, three oxygens. Two carbons have evaporated from the record. Six hydrogens unaccounted for. One oxygen materialised out of thin air. The equation is claiming atoms were created and destroyed — and that breaks the oldest law in chemistry: atoms are only ever rearranged. Fixing it is a shopping rule. The big numbers in front are packets — buy as many as you like. The little numbers inside are the label — locked, because nudge H2O into H2O2 and you have swapped water for antiseptic. So: carbon first — three carbons need three CO2. Hydrogen next — eight hydrogens need four waters. Oxygen last, because it is everywhere — the products demand ten atoms, oxygen travels in pairs, five O2. One propane, five oxygen, three carbon dioxide, four water. Count both sides: three and three, eight and eight, ten and ten. The equation finally tells the truth — and now you can make any equation confess.
visual_style: A chalk equation on a dark board with atoms as glowing counters sliding onto a two-pan balance that visibly tips; red counters blink where atoms go missing, then coefficients stamp down like price tags and the balance levels with a satisfying click.
mood: Detective energy — an innocent-looking line exposed, then set right step by step.
pacing: Sharp accusation open, quick counting beats, methodical three-step fix, clean click-shut ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make the audit your closing move in every exam.
